{"id":"mimid-1wgh.143","title":"Decision: what WHOWAS answers, and where the nick times live","description":"WHOWAS is class 1 of epic mimid-1wgh.140: answerable from the agent's own
facts. Bead mimid-1wgh.140.3 implements it. Five readings had to be settled,
against ~/PROJECT/IETF/specs/ircdocs-modern.html (the Modern IRC Client
Protocol), ~/PROJECT/IETF/specs/ircdocs-modern-numerics.yml for every number,
and ~/PROJECT/IETF/specs/rfc2812.txt sec 3.6.3 where Modern and RFC 2812 differ.

1. WHOWAS ANSWERS FOR A NICK THAT IS STILL IN USE.

Modern :2645 says WHOWAS "asks for information about a nickname which no longer
exists", and 314 RPL_WHOWASUSER (:3574) "shows details about one of the last
clients that used the nickname". A mimid nick is derived from the user URI
alone (names.rs `base_identity`), is given once and is never released, so "no
longer exists" names nothing here.

Reading A: answer for any nick this run has given, saying which MIMI user it
stands for and since when.
Reading B: answer 406 for every nick, because no nick has ever stopped
existing, and so never say anything.

CHOSEN: A. B is conformant and useless; A is the only version of the verb that
has something true to say, which is the whole reason the verb is in class 1 and
not class 2. It is mimid's own deviation from Modern's prose and not a copy of
any reference server: meshIRCd implements no WHOWAS, and Modern's Reply
Examples (:2670-2691) show no server answering for a live nick. The design note
and the crate's # Limitations say so plainly, so the behaviour does not read as
a bug.

2. ONE NICK, NOT A COMMA LIST, AND NO TARGMAX TOKEN.

Modern :2641 gives "Parameters: <nick> [<count>]", one nick. RFC 2812:1866
gives `<nickname> *( "," <nickname> ) [ <count> [ <target> ] ]`.

Reading A: Modern, one nick. `WHOWAS a,b` asks about the nick "a,b", which no
nick can be (`,` is not a nick character), so it is 406 then 369.
Reading B: RFC 2812, split the list, answer the first and drop the rest, as
mimid's WHOIS does.

CHOSEN: A. Modern is this crate's reference, B silently drops a parameter
mimid was not asked to drop, and Modern sanctions dropping excess targets only
where it says so (WHOIS :2604, KICK, NAMES) and says nothing of the sort for
WHOWAS. No TARGMAX token either: Modern's TARGMAX (:5054) is for commands that
take a target list, and WHOWAS does not take one here, so advertising
`WHOWAS:1` would promise a list mimid never reads. RFC 2812's `<target>`
parameter is likewise not read: there is no other server to ask.

3. <count> IS ACCEPTED AND NOT READ.

Modern :2649: "If there are multiple entries, up to <count> replies will be
returned (or all of them if no <count> parameter is given)"; :2651: "If given,
<count> SHOULD be a positive number. Otherwise, a full search is done". RFC
2812:1875 settles the non-positive case the same way: "If a non-positive number
is passed as being <count>, then a full search is done".

mimid holds at most one entry per nick, because `take_nick` is the only place a
nick is bound to a user and nothing ever removes the binding while the daemon
lives. So the reply is one entry or none, which satisfies every value <count>
can take: a positive count is at least 1, and anything else is a full search,
which is that same one entry. Parsing it could only produce a difference where
none exists, so the parameter is read as nothing, and the pointer at
`Session::whowas` says why. This is NOT a licence to drop the parameter once a
persisted history exists (bead mimid-1wgh.140.8): with more than one entry per
nick, <count> and "the history is searched backward, returning the most recent
entry first" (:2648) both start to bite.

4. 312's <server info> KEEPS BEING A SERVER DESCRIPTION, WITH THE TIME ON IT.

Modern :2656 lets a WHOWAS entry carry 312 RPL_WHOISSERVER, and :3556 defines
<server info> as "a string containing a description of that server". inspircd
and solanum put the entry's date there in Modern's own Reply Examples.

Reading A: a bare ISO-8601 timestamp, as those two servers print.
Reading B: the same description mimid's WHOIS 312 already sends,
`mimid-agent`, with the time named in the same parameter.

CHOSEN: B, `mimid-agent; this run has had this nick since <ISO-8601>`. A gives
one numeric two meanings inside one file, since command.rs already sends
`mimid-agent` as 312's server info for WHOIS; and a bare time invites the
reading "when this user was first met", when what mimid knows is when this run
gave or last read the nick. The text is INVENTED, NOT FROM SPEC: Modern fixes
no wording.

5. THE MAPPING LIVES IN `Names`, NOT PER CONNECTION AND NOT IN THE STORE.

Bead mimid-1wgh.140.3 asks for this one to be decided and recorded, and
suggests per connection.

Reading A (the bead's suggestion): per connection, forgotten on reconnect.
Reading B: in `Names`, for the life of the daemon run.
Reading C: in the store, outliving the run.

CHOSEN: B. A buys no confidentiality, because every IRC connection here is the
same user and `Names::user_of` already resolves every nick the run has given,
so WHOIS answers 311 with the user URI for all of them and ISON lists them all;
and it needs a recording call at every rendering site, each one a chance to
miss, where `take_nick` is one function through which every nick passes, so a
history recorded there cannot drift from the mapping it describes. C is the
thing the bead was protecting against and is deferred to mimid-1wgh.140.8 with
its retention question. B keeps the smaller claim: it dies with the daemon and
never becomes a persistent record of whom the user talked to.

NO NEW LIMIT, AND NO SECOND COPY OF THE MAPPING. The time is recorded beside
the mapping, keyed on the folded nick, not in a bounded queue of its own. A
queue would have had to evict, and `Session::who` admits any well-formed
`mimi://<domain>/u/<local>` the client types, so WHOIS of invented URIs mints
entries from the socket with no flood control in front of it (design note:
"Flood control: none on loopback"): an eviction bound would have let a client
push the user's own nick and every contact's out of the history and get 406
where WHOIS still answers. `nicks` and `users` are themselves unbounded from
the same input, which is a pre-existing gap against AGENTS.md's rule that every
count limit is a named constant, and belongs in its own bead; a mirror with an
eviction bound would have bought divergence from the authoritative mapping
rather than a bound.
